analysis:
All units in this batch are test files: Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift (adds a .toolCallDelta case that collects only delta.completed calls), the new StreamedToolCallTests.swift, and NemotronSuperLocalOutputTests.swift (adds a .toolCallDelta case that fails the test). No production code is in the supplied evidence, so the behavior these tests describe is not verified here.

What the tests assert about the unseen production change (early streaming of `auto` tool-call fragments):
- Calls with undeclared names are never exposed. Gemma falls back to text; Harmony completes the call unexposed and then fails validation (StreamedToolCallTests.swift lines 158-180).
- Schema violations are refused when the frame closes (lines 143-156). The name fragment can already be on the wire before the violation is detected. That is a design tradeoff, not a confidentiality regression.
- parallel_tool_calls=false is enforced (lines 182-193).
- Truncated calls end quietly only at the token limit (lines 195-207).
- Forced tool_choice and the nemotron_h family keep the validate-then-expose path (lines 57-78).
- Kill switches DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and the plain-tail seed key must reach the launchd job via LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (lines 82-89).

Threat-model relevance: the streamed fragments are provider-to-coordinator content frames. T-008 (fail-closed encryption of SSE chunks) and the per-chunk encrypt/hash path in ProviderLoop.parseStreamChunk and encodeToolCallsForHash are the relevant contracts. The new tests exercise frame parsing and hashing (lines 319-332) but cannot show that each fragment is encrypted before leaving the provider. The next review pass should check the production ProviderLoop streaming path to confirm every new toolCallDelta frame passes through the same encryption and fail-closed handling as ordinary content.

The tests introduce no new attack surface and no secrets. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is not touched.
